{{short description|Finnish cryptographer}}
'''Kaisa Nyberg''' is a Finnish [[cryptographer]] and [[computer security]] researcher.

==Contributions==
Nyberg's research includes the theory of perfect nonlinear [[substitution box|S-boxes]]{{ran|N}} (now known as Nyberg S-boxes),{{r|ytg}} [[provable security|provably secure]] [[block cipher]] design (resulting in [[KN-Cipher]],{{r|smk}}{{ran|NK}} and the [[cryptanalysis]] of the [[stream cipher]]s [[E0 (cipher)|E0]]{{ran|HN}} and [[SNOW]]{{ran|B+}}).

==Education and career==
Nyberg received her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1980 from the [[University of Helsinki]]. Her dissertation, ''On Subspaces of Products of Nuclear Fréchet Spaces'', was in [[topology]], and was supervised by Edward Leonard Dubinsky.{{r|mgp}}

Nyberg began doing cryptography research for the Finnish Defence Forces in 1987, and moved to [[Nokia]] in 1998. She became professor of cryptology at [[Aalto University School of Science and Technology|Aalto University School of Science]] in 2005, and retired as a professor emerita in 2016.{{r|retire}}

==Recognition==
Nyberg was the 2015 recipient of the Magnus Ehrnrooths Foundation Prize of the Finnish Society of Arts and Letters.{{r|ehrnrooths}}
